source_rows.takeaway: Codex CLI release cadence and platform behavior are changing quickly; launcher and version receipts should stay explicit.
source_rows.x2_use: Keep v6 launch receipts version/launcher-compatible and redacted.

source_rows.takeaway: Codex CLI identity and connector authorization are separate operational surfaces.
source_rows.x2_use: Do not mutate account or connector settings while repairing CLI lane authority.

source_rows.takeaway: Least privilege, constrained transport, and explicit authorization boundaries matter for tool-connected agents.
source_rows.x2_use: Treat app-server routes, CLI lanes, and future context-refresh actions as separate permission classes.

source_rows.takeaway: Agent, model, tool, event, and error telemetry should be named consistently.
source_rows.x2_use: Normalize v6 watcher receipts with lane, phase, boundary, repair_state, quality, and blocker fields.

source_rows.takeaway: Callbacks provide observe/customize/control hooks around model, tool, and agent behavior.
source_rows.x2_use: Model THOS watcher gates as callbacks: prelaunch, cadence, completion, quality, repair, and publication.

source_rows.takeaway: Multi-agent systems need structured composition rather than raw handoff chaos.
source_rows.x2_use: Keep app and CLI siblings as existing lanes with structured receipts, not ad hoc new agents.

source_rows.takeaway: Programmable guardrails can constrain LLM applications at behavior boundaries.
source_rows.x2_use: Keep no-overclaim, raw-boundary, credential/path, and stale-authority guards explicit.

source_rows.takeaway: Guardrail services can be deployed as bounded infrastructure components.
source_rows.x2_use: Treat THOS guard runners as deployable bounded services with receipts and status boards.

source_rows.takeaway: Skills need inventory, permission review, testing, and monitoring.
source_rows.x2_use: Keep skill candidates as overlays unless exact live-skill approval is active.

source_rows.takeaway: Provenance and attestations make artifacts traceable.
